title: Don't open with the banger
hook: Your first record shouldn't be a banger. Here's why.
voiceover: Your first record shouldn't be a banger. Here's why. Saturday, doors at 10, I'm on at 10. The room is 12 people and a bartender. If I open with the biggest record I own, I've told those 12 people the peak already happened and they missed it. What I actually do is open around 95 BPM with a record people know but nobody dances to on purpose. It sets the volume, lets the sound guy hear the system, and tells the people walking in that something is coming. I save the first real record for when there's a line at the bar. That's the room telling me it's ready. What do you open with?
caption: Saturday set building. The opening record has one job: tell the room something is coming without spending it. I open around 95 BPM with something familiar that nobody dances to on purpose, let the system settle, and hold the first real record until there's a line at the bar. The room tells you when it's ready if you're watching. DJs, what's your opener tonight?
